A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the relationship between economic development and class identity is not linear, but instead depends on a country’s degree of income inequality.
economic conditions, especially income inequality, have a significant impact on social class identification, but the effect is moderated by national context and individual characteristics.
the effect of income on class identity is not only dependent on the level of development but also on the level of inequality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of income inequality on social class identification is not limited to the lower end of the income distribution, but also extends to the upper end of the income scale.
economic inequality is a key driver of class consciousness, even in countries where class consciousness is otherwise low.
